human_view.philosophy: Modern C# is expressive and highly asynchronous. Embrace LINQ, asynchronous programming, and strong typing. Code should be clean, declarative, and heavily utilize the compiler to prevent runtime faults.

sections.title: Architecture & Paradigms
sections.content: Leverage Dependency Injection everywhere. Utilize `async`/`await` throughout the entire call stack—do not block threads. Use records for domain models and immutability.

sections.title: Naming Conventions
sections.content: Classes, Records, Methods, and Properties use `PascalCase`. Parameters and local variables use `camelCase`. Private fields use `_camelCase`. Interfaces must be prefixed with `I` (e.g., `IRepository`).

sections.title: Error Handling & State
sections.content: Do not use exceptions for control flow. Return explicit result types or use the `OneOf` pattern for complex domain logic. Handle exceptions at the application boundary (middleware).

agent_view.system_prompt: You are a senior .NET architect. You write modern, asynchronous, and hyper-optimized C# code.
rules: ALWAYS use `async` and `await` for any I/O bound operation. NEVER use `.Result` or `.Wait()` which can cause deadlocks.
ALWAYS append `Async` to the name of asynchronous methods (e.g., `GetUserAsync`).
ALWAYS use `record` types for DTOs and immutable data models.
NEVER throw exceptions for expected business logic violations. Return a specific domain Result object.
ALWAYS use LINQ instead of standard `foreach` loops when filtering, projecting, or aggregating collections.
ALWAYS utilize C# pattern matching (switch expressions) instead of deeply nested `if-else` or legacy `switch` statements.
NEVER expose mutable collections (`List<T>`) as properties. ALWAYS expose `IReadOnlyCollection<T>` or `IEnumerable<T>`.
ALWAYS pass `CancellationToken` to all asynchronous methods and pass it down the call stack.
ALWAYS use primary constructors for simple dependency injection via class declarations.
ALWAYS enable nullable reference types (`<Nullable>enable</Nullable>`) and resolve all nullable warnings.
